displayOrder.name: List and Preview
displayOrder.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a realistic, production-quality PokeTaskBar macOS desktop app ISSUES screen. Continue the approved light Linear-style UI from the actual attached reference images: image 1 is Today, image 2 is Focus. Match their native window, navigation, typography, spacing and quiet surfaces while composing a useful Issues page.
Target 1488 x 1056, same landscape viewport as references, straight-on complete app window. Current date Friday 18 September 2026 if a date is visible. No concept names, numbered labels, annotations, browser frames or marketing content around the app.
Preserve the expanded left navigation approximately 240px wide: PokeTaskBar identity; Cody; Search; Today, Focus, Issues, Projects, Initiatives, Collection, Usage; Settings at bottom. Issues is selected. Keep traffic lights, back/forward, compact Issues page tab and left/right sidebar collapse buttons.
Shared styling: #EFF0F2 continuous window shell behind navigation; #F8F8FA rounded inset main canvas with gutters visible on every edge including bottom corners; white discrete content surfaces only for meaningful groups; text #242528, muted #73757B; restrained blue and yellow status accents, dark primary buttons. SF Pro-like readable 14-16pt UI. Clean outline icons and precise alignment. Absolutely NO permanent sidebar strokes, major section dividers, edge-to-edge horizontal rules or visible resize grip dots. This is the resting state: hover-only resize guides are invisible. Use whitespace and surface changes. Do not outline every issue as a separate card.
Goal: review existing Linear issues and choose one to focus on. Preserve existing destinations In progress and Completed today, a small New issue action, refresh/sync affordance, status changes, readable issue descriptions, project and team context, priority, labels, Open in Linear and Start focus. Keep scope calm: no boards, sprints, burndowns, velocity metrics, AI summaries, rewards or arbitrary new navigation. A local search field 'Find an issue...' may help find a task. No duplicate nav for Issues/Projects/Initiatives inside the page.
Use this small illustrative issue set consistently: SPA-142 'Refine PokeTaskBar navigation'; SPA-148 'Polish menu-bar controls'; SPA-151 'Check sidebar resizing'; SPA-139 'Review focus session notes'; PER-84 'Write weekly reflection'; SPA-133 'Review capture workflow'. All six are In progress, not future tasks. Selected SPA-142 belongs to project PokeTaskBar, team [SPAWN], priority Medium, label Design. Description: 'Keep navigation clear and make room for the current task. Preserve the panel gutters when sidebars resize.' 25 min can be shown beside Start focus. No currently running session, so Start focus is coherent. Subdued small text 'Synced just now'. Task IDs and sample titles are illustrative.
The Pokémon hero remains on Today; do not force a large creature or timer onto Issues. Essential task actions must remain available when the optional right sidebar is hidden. The primary visual hierarchy is the issue list and selected task.

Direction: List and Preview.
Main inset canvas approximately 835px wide. Right sidebar is expanded about 340px wide and contains one rounded white selected-issue preview surface, visually separate from the main panel with a gutter and no separating line.
Main header Issues, subtitle 'Choose a task to focus on'; modest New issue button at top right. Quiet In progress 6 / Completed today tabs, then a small Find an issue field. Below, use ONE clean flat six-row list with no boxed rows: circular yellow state glyph, muted identifier, readable title and small project metadata. Selected SPA-142 has a subtle neutral row background. Give rows 76px height, comfortable type and whitespace. Avoid horizontal separators. The selected row includes a visible compact Start focus action at its far right so it is available even when the inspector is hidden. Bottom main area has a small quiet sync status.
The right preview shows SPA-142, selected task title on two lines, the brief description and neatly aligned Status In progress, Project PokeTaskBar, Team [SPAWN], Priority Medium, Label Design. Use spacing rather than rules between property groups. The preview footer offers Open in Linear as a quiet secondary link. No duplicate large primary CTA in the inspector. Show a calm, highly polished task browser.

Direction: Project Groups.
Organise the Issues page by project context, with compact aligned rows and a clear selected-task action area. Preserve the exact approved shell and expanded left nav. The main rounded inset canvas is wide, about 875px; the optional right extras rail about 295px.
Main top: Issues heading, modest New issue action; In progress 6 and Completed today 0 as restrained tabs using a neutral selected background and no underline rule. Then a compact Find an issue search and 'Group by: Project' control. Content is a flat grouped list on the main canvas with NO per-row cards, NO divider rules. Three collapsible group headings differentiated only by spacing, bold small label and folder icon: 'PokeTaskBar 4', 'Personal 1', 'Workflows 1'. In PokeTaskBar, four 50px rows SPA-142, SPA-148, SPA-151, SPA-139. Personal contains PER-84. Workflows contains SPA-133. Each row has a small status glyph, quiet identifier, readable title, and a tiny aligned priority icon at trailing edge. Selected SPA-142 is tinted neutral.
Near the bottom of the main canvas, a modest separate white rounded selection panel presents 'Selected issue', SPA-142, the task title, and one obvious dark Start focus button with 25 min. This action stays in the main canvas even when the right rail closes.
Right extras are compact separate surfaces: one 'Issue details' panel with Status In progress, Project PokeTaskBar, Team [SPAWN], Priority Medium, Label Design; below, one 'Description' panel with the selected task description and a quiet Open in Linear link. No decorative status metrics, counts beyond actual group counts, or companion. Main panel has generous bottom and side gutters, all section boundaries without strokes; resize guides hidden. Keep typography smaller and rows more compact than a giant task hero, like Linear's task lists, while entirely readable.
